name: StreamBench
intro: StreamBench 是 StreamChat 论文提出的流式视频理解基准，包含 306 段共 24.8 小时的视频和约 1800 组带时间戳问答，覆盖六类多轮在线理解任务。
org: Dalian University of Technology, Harvard University
build_method: 公开视频聚合, 多模态模型分类, 人工筛选与反馈标注
metric: Semantic Score, Accuracy, Coherence, Request Processing Delay
eval_feature: 流式视频前缀, 多轮对话, 六类时间约束问题, 延迟评测
build_method_en: Public-video aggregation, multimodal-model classification, human filtering and feedback annotation
eval_feature_en: Streaming video prefixes, Multi-turn dialogue, Six temporally constrained tasks, Latency evaluation
intro_en: StreamBench is the streaming-video benchmark introduced with StreamChat. It contains 306 videos totaling 24.8 hours and about 1,800 timestamped QA pairs across six multi-round online-understanding tasks.
metric_en: Semantic Score, Accuracy, Coherence, Request Processing Delay
drawio_review_note: Aligned with StreamChat arXiv:2501.13468 Section 2, Section 4.1, and Appendix D; official hmxiong/StreamChat repository. The video StreamBench in Seed1.5-VL is the benchmark introduced with StreamChat, not the namesake continuous-improvement language-agent benchmark. It draws candidate videos from EgoSchema and YouTube-8M, covers egocentric, web, work, and movie domains with 16 subtypes, uses a multimodal model to classify source categories, and has humans remove static or high-noise content. The final 306 videos total 24.8 hours and average 4.5 minutes. Annotators create six timestamped question types per video: object search, long-term memory, short-term memory, conversational interaction, video-grounded knowledge QA, and simple factual QA, each with paper-defined temporal constraints. Different workers check format diversity, clarity and video consistency, and remove sensitive topics. The release contains about 1.8K QA pairs in multi-round streaming dialogues. Models receive only the video prefix available at each query time and the prior dialogue. A LLaMA-3 judge reports semantic correctness score and accuracy; coherence is measured from score fluctuations across turns, and streaming systems also report request processing delay.
